evidence.note: Bury doubts Letter XIII because its presentation of Plato and his relation to Dionysius differs sharply from the stronger Seventh-Letter portrait.
The review of Morrow reports that he was strongly inclined to recognize Letter XIII.
Helfer's 2023 Syracuse analysis treats Letter XIII as part of the designed Platonic sequence and explicitly discusses its self-authentication motifs.

rationale: Letter XIII has long divided scholars. Morrow leaned toward authenticity, while Bury considered its private portrait of Plato difficult to reconcile with the stronger Sicilian tradition and other scholarship has treated it as apocryphal. Helfer's 2023 treatment again integrates it into a Platonic design. Because the positive and negative traditions are both substantial, B best preserves the live dispute.
